feat(csp): delegate 4,191 inline handlers, add a perf budget gate

Content-Security-Policy cannot drop 'unsafe-inline' while the markup carries
onclick= attributes, so this is the first batch of the CSP prerequisite.

Inventory (scripts/audit_inline_handlers.py) over 81 pages:
  call-zero     4,191  (35.2%)  -> migrated here
  call-literal  3,044  (25.6%)  -> next batch, needs argument support
  call-dynamic  3,008  (25.3%)  -> manual rewrite
  expression    1,102  ( 9.3%)  -> manual rewrite
  statement       564  ( 4.7%)  -> manual rewrite

Batch 1 converts on<event>="fn()" to data-sr-call="fn" for the 164 functions
whose bodies provably never touch `this` (delegation binds the same element, so
this check keeps semantics identical). js/sr-events.js provides one
document-level listener for click/input/change/submit/keypress/mousemove.

Two bugs found and fixed while doing it, both caught by existing gates:
  - the first run rewrote handler-looking strings inside script blocks and
    broke 4 pages; the migrator now masks script/style/comment regions
  - the runtime script tag was inserted before the first closing body tag,
    which sits inside JS that builds e-mail templates; it now targets the last
    real one

Guard added: browser_console_audit.mjs now validates data-sr-call targets too,
so moving a handler out of the markup cannot silently lose coverage.

Verified: menu open/close still works on the Arabic and English portals (0
missing handlers, 84 and 70 delegated per page), 30/30 pages console-clean,
7,718 handlers left for later batches.

Also adds scripts/check_perf_budget.py plus a CI step: Lighthouse runs against a
production-like pre-compressed server and fails on payload regressions
(2,200 KB / 55 requests / 400 KB per asset). Current: 1,830 KB, 45 requests.
